title: Uno's no-stacking rule
hook: Under Uno's official rules, you cannot pass a Draw Two along with another.
peek: In 2019 the official Uno account reminded players that stacking a Draw Two on a Draw Two is not in the rules. Thousands of families who had always played that way were surprised, and many said they would carry on anyway.
lede: In many homes, if someone plays a Draw Two on you, you can answer with your own and push four cards onto the next player. It feels like a rule, but it is not one. In 2019 Mattel's official Uno account said so on Twitter: if a Draw Two lands on you, you draw two cards and miss your turn, with no passing it on.

bullets.text: The post drew a flood of replies from players who had stacked for years, many promising to keep doing it. Stacking is a house rule, and plenty of families treat it as part of the game.

The official rules also limit the Wild Draw Four: you may play it only when you hold no card of the current colour. The next player can challenge, and if you were bluffing, you draw the four cards instead.

Uno was invented in 1971 by Merle Robbins, a barber in Reading, Ohio, after a family argument over the rules of Crazy Eights. He sold early decks from his shop before selling the rights, and Mattel took over the game in 1992.
Mattel did eventually make stacking official, but only in a separate edition. Uno Show 'Em No Mercy, released in 2023, lets players stack draw cards on purpose.
